metadata.title: Assessment evidence guide for enterprise IT - Visibility and response OSCAL Resolved Catalog

prop.name: domain-description
prop.value: Procedures and capabilities for detecting, analysing and responding to cyber security events and incidents.

prop.name: resolution-tool
prop.value: OSCAL Profile Resolver XSLT Pipeline OPRXP

remarks.p: Consumers of this file should refer to the Essentials OSCAL NS 1.0 page for information regarding the Essentials specific representation used in this OSCAL file.

part.name: overview
part.p: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data) are continually and centrally identified and documented.

part.name: statement
part.p: Use an approved asset inventory mechanism that supports automated discovery to detect new and changed physical and non-physical assets.

part.name: item
part.p: No approved asset inventory mechanism is in place.

part.name: item
part.p: Asset inventory records are maintained manually with no automated discovery capability.

part.name: item
part.p: An approved asset inventory mechanism is deployed but does not cover all network segments or asset types.

part.name: item
part.p: Automated discovery scans to detect new and changed physical and non-physical assets occur on a schedule but reconciliation with the approved inventory is manual or inconsistent.

part.name: item
part.p: An approved asset inventory mechanism which supports automated discovery is deployed to cover all applicable assets and network segments.

part.name: item
part.p: Discovery runs on a regular schedule defined by the organisation and new or changed physical or non-physical assets that are detected are reconciled with the approved inventory.

part.name: overview
part.p: Security risks for an organisation and their systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are identified, including by using current strategic and sector-specific cyber threat intelligence and threat modelling, and are documented along with any associated risk management decisions.

part.name: statement
part.p: Identify relevant weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours when undertaking risk assessments and review these inputs on a continuous basis.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk assessments do not reference relevant weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours.

part.name: item
part.p: No process exists to incorporate threat information into risk assessment activities.

part.name: item
part.p: Current weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours that are relevant to the organisation are not reviewed or updated.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk assessments reference threat intelligence but coverage is limited to well-known or generic threats.

part.name: item
part.p: Threat information is considered but not systematically mapped to organisational assets or detection gaps.

part.name: item
part.p: Current weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours that are relevant to the organisation are reviewed or updated, but are not used to inform risk assessments or are reviewed only on an ad hoc basis.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk assessments incorporate and reference relevant weaknesses, malicious actor techniques relevant to the sector, and cyber threat behaviours.

part.name: item
part.p: Relevant weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours are systematically related to applicable assets and used to inform risk treatment decisions.

part.name: item
part.p: Current weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours relevant to the organisation are reviewed or updated on a continuous basis at a frequency that enables noted changes to inform risk assessments.

group.title: PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management

part.name: overview
part.p: Robust and secure identity, credential and access management is used to establish, maintain and control access to systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) and to support effective detection of identity and credential misuse.

part.name: statement
part.p: Identify and remediate unsecured keys, secrets and credentials by regularly scanning codebases, configuration files, file shares and user collaboration platforms.

part.name: item
part.p: No secret scanning capability is deployed.

part.name: item
part.p: No process exists to identify credentials exposed in codebases, configuration files, file shares or user collaboration platforms.

part.name: item
part.p: Unsecured keys, secrets and credentials found exposed in codebases, configuration files, scripts, file shares or user collaboration platforms are left in place with no action taken.

part.name: item
part.p: Secret scanning is deployed but does not cover all repositories, pipelines or user collaboration platforms.

part.name: item
part.p: Scanning runs but discovered credentials are not assessed in a timely manner.

part.name: item
part.p: Unsecured keys, secrets and credentials that are discovered are assessed, but are not rotated or revoked in a timely manner.

part.name: item
part.p: Secret scanning tooling is deployed across codebases, configuration files, file shares and user collaboration platforms.

part.name: item
part.p: Scans to identify unsecured keys, secrets and credentials run on a regular schedule defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Unsecured keys, secrets and credentials that are discovered are assessed, then rotated and/or revoked within timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: overview
part.p: Security-relevant event logs and configuration changes for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are centrally collected, protected against unauthorised modification or deletion, and retained to support effective cyber security event detection and investigation.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools

part.name: statement
part.p: Establish a centralised event log storage capability that protects logs from unauthorised access or modification.

part.name: item
part.p: No centralised capability exists for storing event logs collected from systems across the environment.

part.name: item
part.p: Stored logs have no protection against modification or deletion by administrators of the systems generating them.

part.name: item
part.p: Access to the centralised capability is not restricted, or access is granted to roles without a documented need.

part.name: item
part.p: Log retention requirements are not defined.

part.name: item
part.p: A centralised capability exists but does not receive logs from in-scope systems, or coverage is inconsistent.

part.name: item
part.p: Stored logs are protected from modification, but the controls do not consistently prevent deletion, or controls are not applied to all log types.

part.name: item
part.p: Access is restricted to a defined set of roles but access is not logged or monitored.

part.name: item
part.p: A retention period is defined but is inconsistently applied, or some log types are retained for shorter periods than required.

part.name: item
part.p: A centralised event log storage capability is in place for logs collected from in-scope systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Stored logs are protected against unauthorised access, modification and deletion through technical controls including access restrictions, encryption at rest and integrity protection.

part.name: item
part.p: Access to the centralised capability is restricted to security operations personnel and other roles with a documented need, with access logged and monitored.

part.name: item
part.p: Log retention requirements are defined and aligned to investigative, regulatory and contractual obligations, with retention applied consistently across log types.

part.name: overview
part.p: Anomalous or unexpected events and behaviours for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

part.name: statement
part.p: Ensure detection logic identifies unauthorised changes, anomalous authentication activity and suspicious software execution.

part.name: item
part.p: No detection logic is deployed to identify unauthorised changes, anomalous authentication activity or suspicious software execution events originating from assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection relies entirely on manual log review with no automated rules or alerting.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection logic exists but does not cover all three categories (unauthorised changes, anomalous authentication, suspicious execution).

part.name: item
part.p: Rules are deployed but are not tested or tuned on a regular cycle defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection logic is deployed, and unauthorised configuration changes, anomalous authentication patterns and suspicious process execution events are captured and produce alerts.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection logic is tested and tuned on a regular cycle defined by the organisation to maintain effectiveness.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection coverage is reviewed following cyber security incidents or significant environmental changes.

part.name: overview
part.p: Cyber security events are analysed in a timely manner to identify cyber security incidents.

part.name: statement
part.p: Triage alerts and events in a timely manner to determine whether cyber security incident thresholds have been met.

part.name: item
part.p: No documented triage process exists.

part.name: item
part.p: Alerts are routinely ignored or left unreviewed.

part.name: item
part.p: No incident severity thresholds are defined.

part.name: item
part.p: A triage process exists but response times are not defined or consistently met.

part.name: item
part.p: Severity thresholds are defined but escalation procedures are informal.

part.name: item
part.p: A documented triage process with defined severity thresholds and response timeframes is in place.

part.name: item
part.p: Alerts are triaged within the timeframes defined by the organisation and escalated where cyber security incident thresholds are met.

part.name: item
part.p: Triage performance is tracked and reported.

part.name: statement
part.p: Use indicators from across identities, applications, data and infrastructure activity rather than isolated signals when identifying cyber security incidents.

part.name: item
part.p: Investigation relies on single-source alerts with no cross-source correlation.

part.name: item
part.p: Correlation rules do not consider signals from multiple data sources.

part.name: item
part.p: Some correlation exists but is limited to specific data source pairs.

part.name: item
part.p: Cross-source investigation is performed manually but not supported by automated correlation.

part.name: item
part.p: Correlation rules and investigation procedures consider signals across identities, applications, data and infrastructure.

part.name: item
part.p: Automated correlation supports detection of multi-stage adversary activity.

part.name: overview
part.p: Cyber security event detection capabilities are regularly evaluated for effectiveness and continuously refined, including by using current strategic and sector-specific cyber threat intelligence, to improve the detection of cyber security events.

part.name: statement
part.p: Review detection coverage periodically to identify gaps arising from new assets, services or architectural changes.

part.name: item
part.p: No review of detection coverage has been conducted within the period defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: No process exists to assess new assets and services for log coverage or detection applicability.

part.name: item
part.p: A review of detection coverage has been conducted but does not cover all recently deployed assets or services.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection gaps have been identified and remediation is planned, but remediation has not been executed within timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: A detection coverage review has been completed within the cycle defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: New assets and services are assessed for log coverage and detection rule applicability.

part.name: item
part.p: Identified detection gaps are remediated within risk-based timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: overview
part.p: Cyber security incident roles and responsibilities are defined, documented and exercised to support the internal and external coordination and management of cyber security incidents, including responsibilities for declaring cyber security incidents and undertaking pre-approved response and recovery activities.

part.name: statement
part.p: Integrate external coordination obligations into cyber security incident response activities where required.

part.name: item
part.p: External coordination requirements for Cyber security incident response activities are neither identified nor documented.

part.name: item
part.p: No defined triggers, contacts or timeframes exist for external reporting.

part.name: item
part.p: External coordination requirements are documented but are not integrated into operational response procedures.

part.name: item
part.p: Contacts and triggers are defined for some but not all required external parties.

part.name: item
part.p: Cyber security incident response procedures include documented external coordination requirements with defined triggers, contacts and timeframes.

part.name: item
part.p: Requirements cover all relevant external parties identified by applicable legal, regulatory, contractual and organisational obligations.

part.name: item
part.p: Coordination procedures have been exercised or invoked and lessons learnt have been incorporated.

part.name: overview
part.p: Cyber security incidents are contained, eradicated and recovered from in a timely manner.

part.name: statement
part.p: Use documented, tested and approved cyber security incident response procedures when responding to cyber security incidents.

part.name: item
part.p: No documented cyber security incident response plan or procedures exist.

part.name: item
part.p: Incident response activities are conducted on an ad hoc basis without any defined roles, escalation paths, procedures or response objectives.

part.name: item
part.p: Available incident records demonstrate systemic failures to contain, eradicate or recover from cyber security incidents within organisationally defined timeframes, and the causes of these failures are not addressed.

part.name: item
part.p: A cyber security incident response plan exists but has not been exercised or invoked within the organisationally defined test cycle.

part.name: item
part.p: The cyber security incident response plan defines roles, escalation paths, and response procedures, but target timeframes or intended response outcomes are not clearly defined.

part.name: item
part.p: Incident records or exercise results demonstrate that response activities do not consistently meet organisationally defined timeframes or intended outcomes, but identified deficiencies are documented and subject to improvement actions.

part.name: item
part.p: An approved cyber security incident response plan is in place and defines roles, escalation paths, response procedures, target timeframes and intended containment, eradication and recovery outcomes.

part.name: item
part.p: The incident response plan and associated procedures have been exercised or invoked within the organisationally defined test cycle.

part.name: item
part.p: Incident records demonstrate that cyber security incidents are contained, eradicated and recovered from within organisationally defined target timeframes and achieve the intended response outcomes, taking into account incident severity, complexity and business impact.

part.name: item
part.p: Where target timeframes or intended outcomes are not achieved, the causes are analysed, improvement actions are assigned and tracked, and relevant plans, procedures and controls are updated.

part.name: item
part.p: Where no relevant cyber security incident has occurred during the assessment period, appropriately scoped exercises demonstrate the organisation’s capability to achieve its target timeframes and intended response outcomes.

part.name: overview
part.p: Lessons learnt from cyber security incidents are captured, and areas for improvement are identified, prioritised and actioned in a timely manner.

part.name: statement
part.p: Perform post-cyber security incident reviews to identify the security gaps that enabled each stage of the cyber security incident.

part.name: item
part.p: Post-incident reviews are not conducted.

part.name: item
part.p: Post-incident reviews are conducted for some incidents but not all that meet the severity threshold defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Reviews are conducted but findings are not documented or actioned.

part.name: item
part.p: Post-incident reviews are conducted for all incidents meeting the severity threshold defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Findings identify the specific gaps that enabled each stage of the incident.

part.name: item
part.p: Remediation actions arising from findings are implemented and tracked to closure.

part.name: statement
part.p: Evaluate the monitoring coverage and cyber security incident response procedures following cyber security incidents.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection rules, monitoring coverage and response procedures are not reviewed following incidents.

part.name: item
part.p: Reviews are conducted but do not result in documented changes to detection or response capabilities.

part.name: item
part.p: Some improvements are made but not systematically tracked or validated.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection rules, monitoring coverage and cyber security incident response procedures are reviewed following incidents, with identified lessons incorporated into updates.

part.name: item
part.p: Changes are documented, tested and validated for effectiveness.
